item.title: Plenty Of Mobs v1.0.1 Add-On
item.creator: Owls Cubed
item.description:
A natural expansion of your world - familiar mobs, reimagined!
- 200+ NEW VARIANTS, each matched to the biome it lives in
- Every vanilla mechanic kept 100% intact
- 300 HEADS - use a charged creeper to collect them all!
- 200+ PLUSHIES to decorate your base
- Mobs SLEEP at night and DANCE to music discs
- Plus a few all-new monsters in true vanilla spirit
item.changelog:
1.0.1 Polish Update:
+ Add-on monsters no longer spawn in torch-lit places, just like vanilla!
+ Smoother, more natural blinking on every mob!
+ Mob heads fit the player and render right in third person!
+ Cleaner plushie tooltips and other small fixes!

faqEntries.heading: How do I make the mobs dance?
faqEntries.content: Play a music disc in a Jukebox. Every add-on mob within 10 blocks dances while the disc plays.

faqEntries.heading: How do I craft plushies?
faqEntries.content: Craft a Plush Blank from 4 Wool and 4 String, then turn it into any of the 33 plushie families in the Stonecutter. Use a placed plushie to rotate it. Most families have several variants: sneak and hit the plushie to switch to the next one. Plushies with a single variant show no such hint.

faqEntries.heading: Why are the animals lying down?
faqEntries.content: Cows, chickens, ducks, pigs, goats and sheep sleep at night. Sneak to get close without waking them.

faqEntries.heading: How do I breed the new animals?
faqEntries.content: Feed them what their vanilla relatives eat: wheat for cows and sheep, seeds for chickens and ducks, carrots, potatoes and beetroot for pigs.

faqEntries.heading: Do the new mobs replace the vanilla ones?
faqEntries.content: No. Vanilla mobs keep spawning as usual. The new variants spawn alongside them in the biomes they belong to, and every variant has a spawn egg in the Creative inventory.

faqEntries.heading: Why do add-on monsters no longer spawn near my torches?
faqEntries.content: Since 1.0.1 they follow the vanilla rule: no natural spawns where blocks light the ground. Light your base and they stay away, just like vanilla monsters.

item.howToTitle: Getting Started with Plenty Of Mobs

howToEntries.content:
Every player gets the Tutorial Book on their first join. It walks through the biomes, the icons and every mob family. Lost it? Craft a new one from a Book and two Slime Balls. Sneak twice while holding the book to open Bookmarks.

Meeting the mobs: 200+ new variants spawn naturally in the biomes they belong to, next to the vanilla mobs, which keep spawning as usual. Every variant also has a spawn egg in the Creative inventory.

Breeding: feed them what their vanilla relatives eat. Wheat for cows and sheep, seeds for chickens and ducks, carrots, potatoes and beetroot for pigs. Babies grow up on their own.

Sleep and dance: cows, chickens, ducks, pigs, goats and sheep lie down and sleep at night. Sneak if you want to get close without waking them. Play a music disc in a Jukebox and every add-on mob within 10 blocks starts dancing.

Eggs and food: chickens and ducks lay eggs of their own variant. Throw an egg and it can hatch into a chick of that variant, with the same odds as vanilla. Ducks drop Duck Meat and piranhas drop raw Piranha; cook them in a Furnace, Smoker or Campfire. Eaten raw, duck can give you Hunger and piranha can poison you.

Fish: Piranhas, Skeleton Cod and Skeleton Salmon can be scooped up with a Water Bucket and released anywhere else, just like vanilla fish.

Heads: any mob blown up by a Charged Creeper drops its head, add-on mobs and vanilla mobs alike. Wear a head in the helmet slot, or place it on the floor or a wall. On the floor it faces the way you look, in 16 directions.

Plushies: craft a Plush Blank from 4 Wool and 4 String, then put it in the Stonecutter and pick any of the 33 plushie families. Plushies go on floors, walls and ceilings. Use a placed plushie to rotate it. Most families have several variants: sneak and hit the plushie to switch to the next one. Hit it without sneaking to pick it up.

Type /oc_mobs:changelog or /oc_mobs:updates to see what's new in each update.
